rationale: This article examines pedagogical infrastructure, standards, and administrative changes in social work practice learning in England. It is completely unrelated to household or community water or sanitation service access (E01) and measures no water or sanitation access outcomes.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both the narrow rule-type reading and the literal plain reading of Criterion 2 result in exclusion because the article concerns social work education and professional practice learning in England rather than water or sanitation service access (E01).

evidence_quotes.quote: Studying the Landscape: Practice Learning for Social Work Reconsidered
This paper offers a critical analysis of the development and erosion of the infrastructure for practice learning in England over the past two decades.
Although specifically focused on social work it illustrates the way resources can be eroded and so has implications for other professions regulated by government.
